resources.string: Normal adult anatomy. The spongy urethra runs inside the corpus spongiosum, separate from the paired corpora cavernosa. These sections simplify tissue boundaries and omit surrounding structures. The tracer shows direction only, not speed or volume.
In a transverse section, the paired corpora cavernosa lie dorsally. The single corpus spongiosum lies ventrally and encloses the spongy urethral lumen, highlighted in gold.
Urine leaves the bladder through the prostatic urethra, then passes through the short membranous segment before entering the spongy segment. The bend and lengths are schematic.
The spongy urethra continues within the corpus spongiosum to the external urethral opening at the tip. The two dorsal bodies are separate tissues, not channels for urine.
The two larger dorsal bodies are shown in lavender. Neither contains the urethral lumen.
This single ventral body surrounds the spongy urethra. The coral area represents the tissue, not the passage itself.
The gold opening in the transverse section is the lumen. It corresponds to the channel shown along the lower longitudinal section.
The external urethral opening is where the spongy urethra ends and urine leaves the body.
Penis, simplified internal sections: transverse anatomy above and the urinary route below. Not to scale.
